newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipina maid Balabagan drops charges vs agents.
newsitem.headline: Filipina maid Balabagan drops charges vs agents.

text.p: A Filipina maid, who was freed five months ago from a United Arab Emirates jail after being convicted of killing her employer, on Friday dropped criminal charges against the agents who had illegally recruited her.
The teenaged Sarah Balabagan, in an affidavit to the Quezon City Regional Trial court, said she had realised the complaint should not have been filed.
"After all, my desire to work abroad for a better living was the important factor that induced my parents and myself to seek their help," the affidavit said.

Balabagan returned home in July this year after serving three-fourths of her term. She was sentenced to one year in jail, 100 lashes and then deporatation for stabbing to death her 70-year-old Gulf Arab employer, Almas Mohammed al-Baloushi.
An Islamic sharia court rejected her plea that she struck 34 times in self defence as her employer tried to rape her in the July 1994 incident.
The court had earlier condemned Balabagan to death, a sentence which sparked an international outcry.
The sentence was overturned after she agreed to pay the Baloushi family $41,000 in bloodmoney. A Filipino industrialist donated the money to the impoverished Balabagan family.
She got a grand welcome when she returned to the Philippines in August with promises of money as well as movie offers.
The charges against four people, who had recruited her for the job although she was under-age, were filed soon after her return.
Balabagan's affidavit said another reason for her to withdraw the charges was to maintain the relationship with the recruiting agents. They were relatives of the Balabagan family, she said.
State Prosecutor Hilda Sacayclave, who was pursuing the case on behalf of Balabagan, said there was nothing the government could do about her decision to drop the charges.
